name: Runner Extras - Temporary Virtual Table Isolation
brief: Issue #2524: the runner populates system virtual tables (Field 2000000041, Date 2000000007, Aggregate Permission Set 2000000167) into an in-memory store because the service tier computes their rows on the fly. Three of those populates re-run at FIND time, keyed only on the request's table id -- so they also wrote rows into the private store of a `temporary` record of the same table, which must hold exactly what AL put there.
description: The BC-behaviour half of this -- that a `temporary` record round-trips the values AL wrote -- is asserted upstream in the al-language corpus (codeunit 60118), where a real service tier adjudicates it. This suite asserts the runner-specific half: that the runner's own virtual-table populate does not leak into a temporary instance, AND that it still fires for a non-temporary one. The two non-temporary controls that CAN be sensitive were verified to fail against a mutant that makes all three guards unconditional -- that took specific care, because the find-time populates are incremental top-ups layered over the creation-time ones, so the obvious assertions pass even with them disabled: Date must name a range outside the default 1900-2099 window, and Aggregate Permission Set must write its Tenant Permission Set row AFTER the aggregate's first touch. The Field control is NOT sensitive and does not claim to be: nothing in this repository fails when the find-time Field populate is disabled (mutant: 5 runner-extras failures, none Field-related; 0 in the corpus). It is unobserved here -- NOT established as inert; see the test's own comment and #2792 for the unresolved measurement dispute about whether it inserts rows.
